content:
frank: Hey team — trying the docker-compose quickstart from the repo. Followed steps, set REDWOOD_KEY in .env, ran `docker compose up` and the sample returns 402 on first POST even though the web console shows "trial active". Strange part: when I curl the API from my host with the same key it succeeds.

maya: Do you run the container with the env file mounted or baked into the service? Docker can sometimes not pick up updated env files until recreate.

frank: I used `docker compose up --build --force-recreate`. The container prints in logs that it's using a key from `/app/config/.redwood` (masked). I checked that file — it's the old dev key from another account. I definitely set REDWOOD_KEY in the repo .env but the service seems to load the file instead.

julio: That sounds like the compose service has an entrypoint that prefers a file path over env var. Starter should prefer env and log the source. Two separate issues we've seen: (A) config precedence in starter, (B) SDK behavior differences between direct curl and containerized sample.

frank: Reproduced locally: host curl -> 200, container POST -> 402 with response body: {"error":{"type":"billing_required","message":"workspace payment required","billing_url":"https://app.redwood.ai/workspaces/xyz/billing"}}. The host curl shows the same plan active in the console.

maya: Did you confirm the container's token actually matches the host's token? Maybe the host curl uses a user token with an active workspace and the container uses a stale org token.

frank: Yup. I printed both masked tokens side-by-side. Container token source is file; host env token is correct. I replaced /app/config/.redwood with the host token and restarted container. First request then succeeded. So config precedence was the root cause here.

sdk-team: Note: we also saw a parity quirk where older Java SDKs used header `Authorization: Token <key>` and the gateway tolerated it for fully provisioned workspaces but returned 401 or 402 in edge cases while provisioning. Which SDK are you using inside the container?

frank: Starter image includes Java SDK 0.7.8 in the sample microservice. But the curl I ran locally used the CLI (Bearer) from my dev environment. Could be both issues colliding.

julio: Action items: (1) change docker-compose sample to prefer REDWOOD_KEY env var and explicitly log "using key from env" or "using key from file" so users aren't surprised, (2) update Dockerfile to avoid baking a fallback config that contains a stale key, (3) update Java SDK to normalize auth prefix to Bearer and not retry on 402 billing_required.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-131 docker-compose-key-precedence-and-sdk-parity  https://go.redwood.ai/inc/INC-2026-131

frank: For my immediate unblock I added an init step in the compose file that copies /proc/self/environ REDWOOD_KEY into /app/config/.redwood (masked) on startup — ugly but works.

maya: We'll patch the starter repo: prefer env over file and print the chosen source. Also add a note in the onboarding quickstart about waiting ~30s for billing provisioning if you see a 402 right after signup.

starter-bot: Issue opened: redwood-inference/starter#818 "docker: prefer env REDWOOD_KEY over embedded file + log source"

sdk-team: We'll ship Java SDK 0.8.0 with auth prefix normalization and a change to treat 402 as terminal (no automatic retries). Also adding a helper wait_for_workspace_ready(workspace_id, timeout) to the SDK so quickstarts can poll before first request.

frank: Thanks all 144D! After swapping key source and restarting the compose service my first request succeeds. I'll try the PRs and report back if anything else pops up.

sdk-team: Thanks for the clear repro. We'll also include a small troubleshooting blurb in the quickstart README about "Why my container returns 402 but my host curl succeeds".

julio: Closing this thread when starter PR merges and SDK patch is released. Reopen if anyone else sees a similar mismatch.
